claims.excerpt: De POA-refunddienst werd onder tijdsdruk ontwikkeld en ging na twaalf weken publiek.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: “launched to the public in only 12 weeks” and “We had a tight deadline.”
claims.synthesisStatement: The team launched the service publicly in twelve weeks.
claims.narrativeStatement: The service went public after twelve weeks, under time pressure.
claims.explanation: Faithfully reports the deadline context and launch timing.

claims.excerpt: Een aanvankelijk gevraagde levertijd van enkele weken werd niet haalbaar geacht als de gebruikersdienst kwalitatief moest blijven.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: “initially asked to deliver the service in a matter of weeks” and “would not be possible if we wanted to create a quality service for our users.”
claims.synthesisStatement: The requested delivery within weeks was judged infeasible while maintaining quality.
claims.narrativeStatement: The requested few-week deadline was not considered feasible while preserving quality.
claims.explanation: Preserves the source’s qualification that quality was the constraint.

claims.excerpt: De aanpak begon bij de ervaring van aanvragers. Plannen voor caseworkers kwamen later aan bod.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: “focused on the users applying for refunds first”; “Plans for the caseworker user came later.”
claims.synthesisStatement: The team worked first on the applicants’ experience and brought caseworker plans in later.
claims.narrativeStatement: Applicants came first; caseworker work followed later.
claims.explanation: Accurately states the order, though it omits the alpha milestone and the stated reason for that choice.

claims.excerpt: Tijdens de private beta bood een tweewekelijks ritme vaste tijd voor onderzoek en testen, naast het aannemen en verwerken van aanvragen.
claims.label: F2
claims.sourceEvidence: The fortnightly sprints were split in two: week one included testing, research, and accepting applications; submissions were suspended in week two for testing, research, and processing.
claims.synthesisStatement: The two-week sprint had distinct weekly activities, including a week when submissions were suspended.
claims.narrativeStatement: The rhythm reserved research and testing time alongside application work.
claims.explanation: Flattens the specific alternating weekly cadence and omits the suspension of submissions; “naast” can suggest application work ran alongside the reserved research time.

claims.excerpt: Zo zag de beschreven werkwijze eruit: eerst aandacht voor aanvragers, later voor caseworkers, met tijdens de private beta gereserveerde tijd voor onderzoek en testen.
claims.label: F1
claims.sourceEvidence: Applicants were prioritized before caseworker plans; private-beta fortnightly sprints included research and testing.
claims.synthesisStatement: Summarizes the user sequence and the research/testing activity during private beta.
claims.narrativeStatement: Restates the selected approach and its sequencing.
claims.explanation: A broadly faithful recap, but again leaves out the specific week-by-week sprint cadence.

paragraphSteps: Context: time pressure, public launch after twelve weeks, and the quality constraint.
Development: applicants first, caseworkers later, followed by a summary of the private-beta research rhythm.
Recap: repeats the user sequence and research/testing time.
redundancy: Zo zag de beschreven werkwijze eruit: eerst aandacht voor aanvragers, later voor caseworkers, met tijdens de private beta gereserveerde tijd voor onderzoek en testen.
